lines: Chamomile roots on the high meadow grass â€” higher than any apprentice can jump. Pick plenty; soothing burns it up fast.
The bridge goat charges anything it hasn't been soothed for, and a second one guards the path home.
No music? No matter. But goats love music, if your ink runs to a flute.
dialogue_b2_intro.speaker: witch

lines: Two herbs. The goat will dine out on this story for years.
East. The tall grass hums â€” mind it.
dialogue_b2_outro.speaker: witch

lines: Chamomile. Small flowers, soft hands.
Easy, now. Easy.
dialogue_b2_pickup.speaker: apprentice

lines: Fennel grows high past the swarm field. They guard the tall grass jealously.
Time their drifting, or burn fennel to scatter them. Fennel fears no pest.
dialogue_b3_intro.speaker: witch

lines: Three herbs. The field will buzz about you.
The forest edge lies ahead, and something there wears a borrowed shape.
dialogue_b3_outro.speaker: witch

lines: Fennel. Smell that â€” strength itself.
Now, through or around them.
dialogue_b3_pickup.speaker: apprentice

lines: Betony. It waits past the forest edge, where a will-o'-wisp paints false paths.
Trust nothing that shimmers. Burn betony, and walk the real stone.
dialogue_b4_intro.speaker: witch

lines: Four herbs. The charm takes shape.
Rest. The deep forest â€” and plantain â€” will ask harder things of you.
dialogue_b4_outro.speaker: witch

lines: Betony. Against nightmares and false faces.
Now show me what you really are.
dialogue_b4_pickup.speaker: apprentice

lines: Mugwort. Mother of herbs.
One herb for the charm. Now walk it home â€” east, through the door.
dialogue_beat1_pickup.speaker: apprentice

lines: Mugwort first. The potting shed keeps its jars on three high shelves â€” higher than any apprentice can jump, and the herb moves shelf to shelf.
An inch of dust on every jar, and bare hands will only smear it. Conjure a cloth (T), take it (E), wipe with it (U) to read the labels.
Your ink is good for any thing with a name. Speak the noun (T) and pay the ink, and there it stands - ladder, rope, balloon, whatever the moment wants. E takes, U uses - always.
dialogue_level01_intro.speaker: witch

lines: One herb found, eight to go.
The charm is patient. The patient is not â€” back out there soon.
dialogue_level01_outro.speaker: witch

dialogue_trial1.speaker: witch
lines: The patient back home worsens, and only the old charm will mend them - nine healing worts gathered and sung into one salve. That gathering falls to you.
But ere I send you out - hold a moment. Before the jars, before the mud, show me your speaking.
Ink answers any true name, spoken true. Three callings, and I shall know you ready.
First - call me a living thing. Aught with breath. Name it, and let it stand.

dialogue_trial1_done.speaker: apprentice
lines: It breathes! It stands!

dialogue_trial2.speaker: witch
lines: Aye. Breath answers breath. Mind it, though - living things wander, and ink will not leash them.
Second - the high shelf. Your legs will not reach it, so your tongue must. Call what climbs or carries.

dialogue_trial2_done.speaker: witch
lines: Good. The shed is higher than any apprentice. Remember this reaching - the meadow grass grows high as well.

dialogue_trial3.speaker: witch
lines: Third - and mark me well - call a thing of gladness. No use in it at all. Delight alone.

dialogue_trial3_done.speaker: witch
lines: Ha! Even so. A charm sung joyless is but half a charm. Joy is the honey in the salve - never leave it out of your work.
Three callings, three answers. You are ready. Now - mugwort first. The jars wait, dusty as ever.
